input.summary: Meridian runs 13 on-prem production platforms; AWS/Databricks remain aspirational with no certified medallion foundation.
covers: Contact center transcript and telephony platform

story.meaning: Meridian's production estate is entirely on-prem and fragmented; the cloud target state is a declared direction, not an operational platform.
story.observed: 12 active platforms span Epic, SQL Server marts, SAS, Tableau, Power BI, claims, pharmacy, CRM, contact center, GL, and provider contracts — all on-prem. AWS and Databricks are catalogued as aspirational with no certified medallion architecture, no identity spine, and no production analytics workloads.
story.matters: Every top-five use case — lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, payment integrity, cost transparency, call center optimization — requires a certified cloud data foundation that does not yet exist. The gap is not a tooling choice; it is the single largest blocker across the entire Nexus roadmap.
story.supports: Closing this gap requires sequenced evidence gates: AWS/Databricks network and IAM foundation first, medallion architecture certification second, then identity spine and domain data onboarding — before any use case can exit planning stage.

findings: 13 platforms are evidenced as current-core or active; zero cloud platforms are certified production — the entire analytics modernization roadmap sits on an unproven foundation.

On-prem SQL Server marts are rated critical lifecycle status 'fragmented_reporting_estate,' meaning duplicated business rules and extract chains are actively compounding technical debt across BI, finance, and clinical reporting.

AWS analytics foundation and Databricks on AWS are both rated 'aspirational_not_ready' with only planned integrations — no S3, Unity Catalog, or Delta workloads are certified, blocking all five priority use cases from advancing beyond planning.

SAS analytics estate is the current payment integrity detection platform but carries no governed model lineage, making leakage quantification and CFO-level recovery reporting impossible without remediation.

relationships.note: Infrastructure is the root dependency for every Meridian use case. No use case can advance to decision grade until the AWS/Databricks foundation is certified and at least one domain data product clears the medallion evidence gate.

evidence.name: Epic Core Platform Bundle
evidence.facts: Epic Hyperspace, Clarity, and Caboodle are all current-core, high-confidence, and critical. Clarity and Caboodle are the primary clinical data sources for any medallion onboarding.
evidence.supports: Confirms Epic as the anchor clinical source; Clarity ETL is the first medallion ingestion candidate.
evidence.missing: No certified Clarity-to-medallion ETL evidence; Cogito BI integration not yet governed.

evidence.name: On-prem SQL Server Reporting Marts
evidence.facts: Rated critical criticality, medium confidence, lifecycle status 'fragmented_reporting_estate.' Integrations include SSIS, SQL Agent, Tableau extracts, Power BI gateway, and SAS feeds.
evidence.supports: Confirms technical debt severity; duplicated business rules are a direct blocker to semantic layer certification.
evidence.missing: No mart inventory count, no decommission timeline, no rule canonicalization evidence.

evidence.name: Claims and Pharmacy Platform Bundle
evidence.facts: Claims administration is critical/current-core (medium confidence); pharmacy claims is high/current-core (high confidence). EDI and NCPDP feeds are the integration paths.
evidence.supports: Both platforms are production-ready sources; harmonization into a unified claims/pharmacy domain is the next required evidence gate.
evidence.missing: Claims and pharmacy harmonization not proven; no adjudication-to-medallion pipeline evidenced.

evidence.name: AWS Analytics Foundation
evidence.facts: Rated critical criticality, high confidence, lifecycle status 'aspirational_not_ready.' Integrations are planned network/security/IAM only; no production analytics workloads.
evidence.supports: Confirms cloud foundation is a declared strategic direction with critical priority rating.
evidence.missing: No network, IAM, or security foundation certification; no production data workloads evidenced.

evidence.name: Databricks on AWS
evidence.facts: Rated critical criticality, high confidence, lifecycle status 'aspirational_not_ready,' candidate status. Planned S3/Unity Catalog/Delta integration only; no certified medallion architecture.
evidence.supports: Confirms Databricks is the target lakehouse engine; Unity Catalog is the intended governance layer.
evidence.missing: No bronze/silver/gold data products certified; no medallion architecture evidence loaded.

evidence.name: SAS Analytics and Provider Contract Repository
evidence.facts: SAS is current-core for payment integrity models but integrates via flat files with no governed lineage. Provider contract repository is current-manual with document-based terms and manual extracts.
evidence.supports: Identifies the two highest-risk legacy platforms for cost transparency and payment integrity use cases.
evidence.missing: SAS model registry absent; contract digitization not initiated; neither platform has a governed data product.
